name: soapyhackrf
why: A SoapySDR plugin for HackRF, a fine radio door but mostly glue between hardware and the SDR stack.

brief.what_it_is: SoapyHackRF is a plugin module that lets the HackRF software-defined radio be used through the SoapySDR API, and through any software that speaks SoapySDR. It is built with CMake against libhackrf and SoapySDR, and installs into the SoapySDR modules directory. Once installed, SoapySDR tools can probe the device and report its channels, gain stages, frequency range and sample rates. The wiki's probe example shows a HackRF One with one RX and one TX channel, sample rates from 1 to 20 MHz, and a frequency range of 0 to 7250 MHz.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it simply as providing 'a plugin module to use the Hack RF device within the SoapySDR API and software that supports SoapySDR.' It is a driver adapter, so HackRF hardware can be used by the wider SoapySDR-aware software ecosystem without each application writing its own HackRF code.
brief.how_it_works: The module sits between libhackrf, which talks to the hardware, and SoapySDR, the abstraction library that applications call. The CMake build finds the libhackrf and SoapySDR development files on the system and installs the resulting plugin where SoapySDR looks for modules. Applications then open the device through SoapySDR's generic interface rather than HackRF-specific calls.

brief.install_notes: Prerequisites are libhackrf (https://github.com/mossmann/hackrf/wiki) and SoapySDR (https://github.com/pothosware/SoapySDR/wiki). On Ubuntu, the hackrf and libhackrf-dev packages come from the myriadrf drivers PPA. Pre-built installers for Windows, OSX and Ubuntu are distributed through the Pothos SDR environment rather than Homebrew. Building from source needs git, CMake, make and a C++ toolchain, which the wiki implies but does not list. A HackRF must be attached to probe it, and the wiki does not describe udev or USB permission setup.
brief.standout: It is thin glue rather than a radio application: its job is to make HackRF look like every other SoapySDR device, so one probe command or one application works across many SDR front ends. The wiki's probe output is a useful, literal picture of what the HackRF exposes through the abstraction.
brief.status: Quiet, with thin evidence. The wiki home page was last edited by Josh Blum on Sep 8, 2017, and the probe sample reports version 2015.07.2. The repository README is short and shows no release date or recent activity, and I did not check commit history. Treat it as maintained at a low level, not actively developed.
brief.caveats: The README is minimal and the wiki is the real documentation, and parts of it look dated (2015 and 2017 material). Installation steps are Ubuntu-specific for the PPA, and no other distro, macOS or Windows source build steps are given. The probe output is a sample from one device and an old SoapySDR version, so current output will differ. The MIT license is stated in the README with a 2015 copyright line.
